resolved_conflicts.explanation: The nomination's OCR text gives the first assistants as David P. Holeomou and Luther K. Kolomo; the USLHS roster gives Daniel P. Haleamau and Luther K. Kalama. Story uses USLHS spellings.
Nomination dates Stanley Huntington's command 1949-1954; USLHS roster has 1949-1957. Story states both.
Putnam (1917) gives 216 ft above water, the nomination 217 ft; record's 53 m is about 174 ft.
The nomination gives July 1912 (6 or 8 July in different places); The Garden Island of 6 May 1913 says the lighthouse was begun in August 1912. Story states both.

notes_for_editor: Mostly one long source (the NRHP form, poorly OCR'd; names such as Platt/Plott/Piatt, Holeomou, Kopao, Anahola read from scan) plus Lighthouse Service Bulletins. Claude Platt matched to USLHS Claude E. Platt (2nd asst 1939-1942) by name and year only; not merged in the roster. Disagreements: Edgecomb's landing and horseback distance (nomination vs LighthouseFriends); lens out of service 1974 vs 1976; Huntington dates. Whether the 1976 beacon still shows a light today is unconfirmed. Keepers roster left to the generated USLHS table: no keeper entries here to avoid duplicating. Newspaper search (Chronicling America, Hawaii) was started but not completed. Recreation.gov listing still said tours suspended; FWS/Friends 2026 pages say repairs finished but do not say interior tours resumed. Fact-check 2026-10-22: opening claim that a smaller beacon guides ships today was unsupported and reframed to the sourced 1976 change; whether that beacon still shows is unconfirmed.
